clue.text: Come before quiet official, almost give up

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for official is left off

parts.note: a ref is short for referee, a match official
to cede is to give up or yield

explanation.surface: Someone arrives ahead of a softly-spoken official who is on the verge of quitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede something is to go ahead of it in time or order, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Choppy brine covers new motorway and one group of fens

indicators.note: and adds the final letter at the end
covers means the churned letters go around the next pieces
choppy, like rough water, means the letters of brine are churned

parts.note: M is the British abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Rough sea water floods a motorway and drowns part of the Fens.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are low-lying land in eastern England, but a fen is also a hundredth of a Chinese yuan.
explanation.definitionFit: The renminbi is China's currency, whose yuan divides into a hundred fen.

clue.text: Tea, bit of butter all but oblige bread

parts.note: cha (or char) is slang for tea
a pat is a small piece of butter

indicators.note: all but means the last letter of the word for oblige is dropped

parts.note: to tie is to bind or oblige

explanation.surface: A tea-time order: a cup of tea and some butter, almost obliging, with bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapatti is a flat unleavened Indian bread.

clue.text: Home, about to be supplanted by underworld in contention

indicators.note: to be supplanted by means one piece is replaced by another

parts.note: a residence is a home
re means about, as in business letters
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself

explanation.surface: A household is in turmoil, its place taken over by criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld' suggests gangsters, but here it is Dis, the classical underworld, which takes the place of RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissidence is disagreement or dissent, so it is a state of contention.

clue.text: Battle supplies hidden by retreating commander

indicators.note: retreating means the concealed letters are read backwards
hidden by means the letters sit inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: An officer in retreat is concealing military stores.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo is informal for ammunition, the supplies fired in combat.

clue.text: Speaker for a Tory's selection

indicators.note: selection means a run of letters is picked out from the words before it

explanation.surface: A Conservative party chooses its Speaker of the House.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is a public speaker, especially an eloquent one.

clue.text: Quiet drink, boozer's fourth, produces sentimental singing

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a malt is a malt whisky

indicators.note: fourth takes the fourth letter of boozer's

explanation.surface: A quiet tipple in the pub brings on soppy songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is excessive sentimentality, especially in music.

clue.text: Raises a stink, abandoning tango with police officer

indicators.note: abandoning means the letter for tango is dropped from the smell

parts.note: a scent is a smell, here a stink
Tango is the radio code word for T
DS is a Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss, leaving a dance partner for a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raises a stink' reads as one phrase, but 'Raises' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascends means goes up or climbs; taken loosely, rises or raises itself.

clue.text: Game ended early after Border's returning smears

indicators.note: after puts the game's letters behind the reversed borders
returning means the word for borders is read backwards

parts.note: rims are borders or edges

indicators.note: ended early means the game's final letter is cut off

parts.note: chess is the board game

explanation.surface: A match is stopped early once a Borders side comes back, leading to mud-slinging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border's' is capitalised to suggest the Scottish Borders region, but it simply gives RIMS, which turned back is SMIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To besmirch or smirch a reputation is to sully it, so smirches are smears or stains.

clue.text: Cycling soldiers cut off fools in a group

indicators.note: cycling means the first letter of the word for soldiers moves round to the end

parts.note: men are soldiers, as in officers and men

indicators.note: cut off means the last letter of the word for fools is removed

parts.note: asses are fools

explanation.surface: Troops on bicycles separate some idiots from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' moves the M of MEN to the end to give ENM; ASSES loses its last letter to give ASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase en masse means all together, as a whole body of people.

clue.text: Advance made more attractive when little interest is shown?

definitions.text: Advance made more attractive when little interest is shown?

parts.words: Advance made more attractive when little interest is shown?
parts.note: an advance is a loan; a home loan looks better the lower its interest rate, though 'little interest' suggests indifference

explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' reads as attention, as if a suitor plays hard to get; in fact it is the rate charged on a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A home loan from a bank or building society is an advance whose appeal rises as the interest rate falls.

clue.text: Princes' mother keeps housing prince

definitions.note: the possessive plural; the answer is the plural noun

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: housing means the next piece is put inside

parts.note: has means keeps or holds
a raja is an Indian prince

explanation.surface: A royal mother gives a home to a young prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Maharajas were great Indian kings or rulers, high-ranking royals.

clue.text: Iliad rewritten to include western festival

indicators.note: to include means the shuffled letters take the abbreviation inside
rewritten means the letters of Iliad are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Homer's epic is turned into a cowboy story for a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights held in autumn.

clue.text: Dry, heated up and ultimately arid

indicators.note: up means the letters of the two words are stirred or disturbed into a new order
ultimately takes only the final letter of and

explanation.surface: A list of what happens to something left in the heat: dried, warmed, finally parched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like the definition, but it is part of the anagram with HEATED and the D ending 'and'; the definition is 'arid' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dehydrated has had its water removed, so it is parched and without moisture.

clue.text: Disperse protest, anger spreading around island

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: spreading around means the anger goes round the island

parts.note: bile is anger or ill temper

explanation.surface: A protest breaks up as fury spreads across an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To demobilise troops is to release them from service, scattering the army.

clue.text: Sadly, a journalist wrote this old piece

parts.note: a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A reporter has turned out an article that is past its best.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a newspaper notice about someone who has died, hence the sad writing.

clue.text: Working soldier sent back driver with American airhead

indicators.note: with joins the final piece on
sent back means the letters for working and soldier are read backwards

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
GI is an American soldier
a ram drives things, as a battering ram or pile-driving ram

explanation.surface: A busy serviceman packs off a chauffeur and his American scatterbrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns both working and soldier round together; a ram is something that drives, like a pile driver or battering ram.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person, close in sense to a fool or empty-headed person.

clue.text: Expression of dismay's no good for women's power

indicators.note: for means one piece stands in for another

parts.note: strewth is an exclamation of dismay or surprise
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: An exclamation that women's power is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength is physical might or force.

clue.text: Detested sailor scraped around bishop

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: around means the scraping word goes round the bishop

parts.note: hoed means scraped the soil with a hoe
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A sailor who scratched a bishop was hated.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop is the Right Reverend, abbreviated RR.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorred means hated intensely, loathed.

clue.text: Bill steals, according to hearsay, legendary creature

indicators.note: according to hearsay means the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: a fee is a bill or charge; nicks is British slang for steals

explanation.surface: Rumour says a man named Bill steals a mythical beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The phoenix is a mythical bird that rises again from its own ashes.

clue.text: Subdues child one's taken on

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a stepchild inherited by marrying a parent

explanation.walkthrough: Split as STEPS ON, the answer is a verb for crushing; whole, it is a son acquired by marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a partner's son from an earlier relationship, a boy taken on through marriage.

clue.text: Type of horn found in Timbuktu backwater

indicators.note: found in means the answer sits within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a sort of horn in a sleepy corner of Timbuktu.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the large, low-pitched brass instrument, loosely one of the horns in a band.

clue.text: Hero, at first hot, abject in ordering assassination

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of hero
ordering means the letters of hot and abject are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A champion, first fevered and then wretched, sets up a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assassination' is meant in the sense of character assassination, a savage attack on someone's reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchet job is a vicious written or spoken attack, so it amounts to character assassination.

clue.text: Frequently sanctimonious about universal right

indicators.note: about means the pious word goes around the next pieces

parts.note: holy, as in holier-than-thou, means sanctimonious
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: Someone sanctimonious keeps going on about universal rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Hourly means every hour, so very often or repeatedly.

clue.text: Vices discovered, confine in cooler

indicators.note: discovered means the outer letters are removed, uncovering the inside of vices

parts.note: to box someone in is to confine them

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing exposed, the culprit is locked up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' is slang for a jail, which fits the surface; here it means something that keeps food cold.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is an old-fashioned refrigerator, a container that chills food.

clue.text: Clarifies what Slimmer of the Week's previous reading shows?

definitions.text: what Slimmer of the Week's previous reading shows?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split 2,6: the pounds a dieter used to weigh are now former pounds

explanation.walkthrough: Slimmer of the Week is the prize at a slimming club; the earlier reading on the scales shows weight now lost, which is read as EX POUNDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound a theory is to set it out and explain it in detail.

clue.text: Force tense after row

indicators.note: after places the tense letter behind the noise

parts.note: a din is a row, a loud noise
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Pressure builds as nerves fray following an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Dint means power or effort, surviving mainly in the phrase 'by dint of'.

clue.text: Critical trap Gerald heartlessly produces

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter of the pet name is removed

parts.note: Gerry is a pet form of Gerald

explanation.surface: A man called Gerald cruelly sets a snare that has serious results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Critical' looks like it means vital, but here it means fault-finding.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingery here means sharp and touchy, in the sense of a stinging or fault-finding manner.

clue.text: Is old country singer in area of rock that's folded?

parts.note: Patsy Cline was an American country singer

explanation.surface: A question: is a veteran country star found in some rocky region?
explanation.definitionFit: In geology an isocline is a fold whose limbs are parallel, so a region of folded strata.

clue.text: Satisfied tool's procedures

parts.note: met means satisfied, as in met a requirement
a hod is a bricklayer's carrying tool; the 's adds an S

explanation.definitionFit: Methods are ways of doing things, systematic approaches or procedures.
